transcript:
This message comes from Angie. Angie has been helping homeowners find skilled pros
to get their home projects done well for over 30 years. For everything from minor repairs
to major remodels, find reviews, pricing, and booking at Angie.com or on the Angie app.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Rylan Barton. President Trump and Vice President J.D.
Vance are hitting the campaign trail to try and boost Republican enthusiasm ahead of the midterm
elections. Vance was in Florida promoting Republican candidate for governor Byron
Donalds and Senator Ashley Moody. He said Democratic Senate candidate Angie Nixon
should leave the country. When Angie Nixon calls herself a socialist, I think the right response
is to say then get the hell out of here. You don't belong in America, if those are your views.
Trump is in Oklahoma now after traveling to Texas as polls show him losing support from
key groups he made inroads with in 2024 like Latinos. Trump has blamed poor public relations
for the party's challenges. Democrats say Trump and Vance are desperate to rally their base as
the elections approach. 21 states are suing the Trump administration over its repeal of power
plant pollution rules. As NPR's Julia Simon reports, the Biden-era rules would have reduced
planet heating emissions from fossil fuel burning plants. The 21 states and four cities argue their
appeal "guts one of the country's most significant climate protections" and will worsen the climate
crisis. The Biden-era rules would have required coal and new natural gas plants to install
pollution control equipment that would have significantly reduced carbon dioxide emissions.
When the EPA announced the rule change last month, they said in their announcement that
greenhouse gas emissions from power plants "have no material impact on climate change."
That is false. And pollution from power plants also impacts human health. The EPA says it doesn't
comment on ongoing litigation. Julia Simon, NCAR News. The Supreme Court has agreed to review
a Trump administration policy denying bond hearings for detained immigrants. The high
court will consider whether immigrants have a right to a hearing to determine if they should
remain detained while challenging their possible deportation. Appeals courts from 9 of 11 federal
circuits have ruled that detention without a bond hearing violates federal law. The judge in the
Lindsay Clancy case has rejected a defense request to find her not guilty of killing her three
children in 2023. That's after the case ended in a mistrial last month from member station WBUR
Deborah Becker reports. Judge William Sullivan's decision says that prosecutors offered enough
evidence for a jury to decide whether Clancy committed the crimes and whether she was criminally
responsible. Clancy's defense asked for the not guilty finding, arguing that prosecutors did not
provide enough evidence. Attorney Keith Halpern, who's not affiliated with Clancy's case,
says defense attorneys customarily make such requests. It was something that any lawyer
in his position would have done in any case. Prosecutors are still evaluating whether to hold
a new trial. Another hearing is scheduled next month. For NPR News, I'm Deborah Becker in Boston.
Major U.S. stock indexes rose slightly today. This is NPR News.
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney is fast tracking an oil pipeline to the Pacific coast.
The move aims to reduce Canada's dependence on the U.S. and mend relations with Alberta,
where separatists are pushing for a referendum on leaving Canada. The pipeline would allow
Canada to export more oil to Asia, reducing reliance on the U.S. Protests by French high
schoolers demanding better learning conditions have turned violent, with nearly 2,000 arrests,
schools and vehicles set on fire and at least 300 police and firefighters injured.
NPR's Eleanor Beardsley reports 400 schools across the country will be closed tomorrow.
A protest against rundown buildings and overcrowded classrooms started last week in
one high school in the Paris suburbs before spreading to more than 1,000 schools across
the country. The students' demands were seen as legitimate, but scenes of chaos and confrontations
between police and massed bands of young people shown on the TV news are shocking the French.
The prime minister, who organized a crisis cell Thursday, has accused the far left of
encouraging the protesters for political reasons. But even far left leader Jean-Luc
Mettenchamp, who has supported the protesters, seemed overtaken by the violent turn of events.
He called on the young people to stop the destruction, saying, "It serves no purpose."
Eleanor Beardsley in Pierre news, Paris.
French soccer star Zinedine Zidane famously headbutted Italy's Marco Maturazzi during the
2006 World Cup final, ending his career with a red card. 20 years later, Zidane will face
Italy again tomorrow, but this time as France's head coach in the Nations League. This is NPR.
Stay tuned for the following announcements and messages from our sponsors.

21 states sue Trump administration over repeal of Biden-era power plant pollution rules
Supreme Court agrees to review Trump policy denying bond hearings for detained immigrants
Judge rejects defense request for not guilty verdict in Lindsay Clancy infanticide case
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney fast tracks oil pipeline to Pacific coast
French high school protests over learning conditions turn violent with nearly 2,000 arrests
Zinedine Zidane faces Italy as France head coach in Nations League match tomorrow
